punchline: Warren Buffett closed a deal worth about $23 billion with a handshake, because both sides had decades of trust behind them.
thirty_sec: In 2003, Berkshire Hathaway bought McLane Distribution, a business of about $23 billion, from Wal-Mart. Instead of months of audits and lawyers, there was one two-hour meeting and a handshake. Buffett did no due diligence, and the deal closed in 29 days. Stephen M. R. Covey uses it to show that trust is economic: high trust means more speed and lower cost. But that speed rested on decades of reputation.
question: Which part of your work would move twice as fast if you fully trusted the people involved?
